claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons exhibit significant internal strain.
As-deposited nanoscale non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons exhibit pronounced surface effects.
Thermal annealing can relieve internal strain while preserving the nanoscale geometry.
Internal strain disrupts magnetic-domain formation and mobility in these alloys.
Surface-induced atomic clustering disrupts magnetic-domain formation and mobility in these alloys.
Internal strain and surface effects impair long-range magnetic interactions in the as-deposited state.
Impaired long-range magnetic interactions weaken coupling between magnetic and lattice responses.
Annealing-induced strain relief restores magnetic-domain-wall mobility.
Annealing-induced strain relief restores coherent magnetostructural coupling.
Restored domain-wall mobility and magnetostructural coupling increase the magnetocaloric temperature change.
Restored domain-wall mobility and magnetostructural coupling reduce magnetic hysteresis.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films have a diminished magnetocaloric response relative to bulk material.
As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films have greater hysteresis than bulk material.
Using sufficiently slow cooling-cycle frequencies avoids heat-transfer-rate limitations.
The magnitude of annealing-induced improvement depends on the annealing parameters and degree of strain relief.
